reconcile.note: Adam Clarke reads the chapter as describing two separate memorials, twelve stones raised at Gilgal and a second twelve left standing in the riverbed itself.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Benjamin Kennicott catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Benjamin Kennicott, The State of the Printed Hebrew Text of the Old Testament Considered (Dissertation the First) (1753).

sides.snippet: Joshua set up twelve stones in the midst of the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests who bore the ark of the covenant stood: and they are there to this day.
sides.verseText: Joshua set up twelve stones in the midst of the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests who bore the ark of the covenant stood: and they are there to this day.

sides.snippet: Those twelve stones, which they took out of the Jordan, did Joshua set up in Gilgal.
sides.verseText: Those twelve stones, which they took out of the Jordan, did Joshua set up in Gilgal.
